name: 10198-specdecode-70b8b-4gpu
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3 of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4).
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, one node, one in-process engine; the draft worker runs in the same worker process and inherits the target's TP.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1, bounded at 500 requests / 7200 s safety, warmup the first 5% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, `request_format: plain`. Prompt exactly 1024 tokens and output exactly 128, with ignore_eos forced by the backend; per-request sampling temperature=0.6, top_p=0.9, top_k=-1, repetition_penalty=1.0.
purpose: A 70-billion-parameter assistant with a draft model, serving one user long single-turn prompts with short replies on four GPUs.
launch:
# Engine command line: commit 0a4d96850013eb2c295b25df53177ad2302110ca, four H100s of one
# node, a 70B target with an 8B speculative draft at K=3.
#
# Flat `key: value` only. An indented line is skipped, so a structured value must stay on ONE
# line or the key is dropped and the engine starts without it.
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-70B
speculative-model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B
num-speculative-tokens: 3
tensor-parallel-size: 4
dtype: bfloat16
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.80
use-v2-block-manager: true
enable-prefix-caching: false
# The workload is a fixed 1024-in / 128-out at one stream, so 1152 tokens is the whole of it and
# at most K+1=4 rows are ever resident. Both keys below only shrink one-time bring-up -- the
# profiling forward and the set of CUDA-graph batch sizes captured -- and neither changes the
# graph the measured decode actually runs (batch 4, captured under both settings).
max-model-len: 2048
max-num-seqs: 8
